{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Kitakyushu|ja|北九州市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitakyushu|qq=}}{{ill|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu|ja|小倉南区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu|qq=}}{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of {{ill|Sect Shinto|ja|教派神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sect Shinto|qq=}} founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around {{ill|Kokura|ja|小倉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokura|qq=}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} on {{ill|Kyushu|ja|九州|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu|qq=}}, Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of {{ill|Koshintō|ja|古神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koshintō|qq=}}.
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from {{ill|Ontake-kyō|ja|御嶽教|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake-kyō|qq=}} in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenominakanushi|qq=}} to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the {{ill|Restoration Shintō|ja|復古神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Restoration Shintō|qq=}} category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.

{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Kitakyushu|ja|北九州市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitakyushu|qq=}}{{ill|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu|ja|小倉南区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu|qq=}}{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of {{ill|Sect Shinto|ja|教派神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sect Shinto|qq=}} founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around {{ill|Kokura|ja|小倉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokura|qq=}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}} on {{ill|Kyushu|ja|九州|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu|qq=}}, Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of {{ill|Ko-Shintō|lt=Ko-Shintō|lt=Koshintō|ja|古神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koshintō|qq=}}.
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from {{ill|Ontake-kyō|ja|御嶽教|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake-kyō|qq=}} in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amenominakanushi|qq=}} to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the {{ill|Restoration Shintō|ja|復古神道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Restoration Shintō|qq=}} category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}

{{Distinguish|Aum Shinrikyo}} {{Expand Japanese}}
{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}
== Bibliography == (Original references retained as-is)
== External Links == * [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō Official Website]{{Ja icon}} * [http://www.sinri-y.ed.jp/ Shinri Kindergarten] * [http://sinri.sub.jp/ Shinrikyō Supporters' Website]

{{Distinguish|Aum Shinrikyo}} {{Expand Japanese}}
{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}
== Bibliography == (Original references retained as-is)
== External Links == * [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō Official Website]{{Ja icon}} * [http://www.sinri-y.ed.jp/ Shinri Kindergarten] * [http://sinri.sub.jp/ Shinrikyō Supporters' Website]

{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.

He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}

{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[:en:Aum Shinrikyo|Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}
== Bibliography == (Original references retained as-is)

{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[:en:Aum Shinrikyo|Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.

He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[:en:Aum Shinrikyo|Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[:en:Shinto Taikyo|Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
== References == {{Reflist|2}}

It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[:en:Aum Shinrikyo|Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[:en:Shinto Taikyo|Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>

==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=|1=Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489547}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=|1=Tsunehiko Sano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385093}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=|1=Tsunehiko Sano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385093}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.

{{nihongo|{{ill|Shinrikyo|ja|神理教|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinrikyo|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|神理教|4=lit: divine principle}} is a [[Sect Shinto]] group founded by {{ill|Tsunehiko Sano|ja|佐野経彦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunehiko Sano|qq=|1=Tsunehiko Sano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385093}}.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sano Tsunehiko and "Divine Principle (Shinri)" |url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/inoue.html |access-date=2023-03-05 |website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=日本国語大辞典,百科事典マイペディア,デジタル大辞泉,世界大百科事典内言及 |first=ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典,日本大百科全書(ニッポニカ),精選版 |title=神理教(しんりきょう)とは？ 意味や使い方 |url=https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A5%9E%E7%90%86%E6%95%99-82712 |access-date=2023-03-12 |website=コトバンク |language=ja}}</ref> It was founded in 1880<ref>https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9780691221298-014/pdf</ref><ref name=":1" />
He had previously studied medicine and was an advocate of traditional Japanese medicine. He studied [[:en:Kokugaku|Kokugaku]] in his youth under Nishida Naokai<ref>https://rks.accesson.kr/assets/pdf/2564/journal-23-1-211.pdf</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9473</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9483</ref>
It is one of the thirteen shinto sects.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=Kyōha Shintō {{!}} Japanese religion |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kyoha-Shinto |access-date=2023-03-06 |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en}}</ref>
The name is relatively common among Shinto groups and does not stand out<ref name=":0" /> [[:en:Aum Shinrikyo|Aum Shinrikyo]] uses different characters in its name though.
It is considered in the [[Fukko Shinto]] lineage of [[Sect Shinto]] alongside [[:en:Shinto Taikyo|Shinto Taikyo]] and [[Izumo-taishakyo]].{{Sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}} It is among the thirteen shinto sects.<ref>{{Cite book |last=井上 |first=順孝 |title= |date=April 1991 |publisher=弘文堂 |isbn=978-4335160219 |page=11 |script-title=ja:教派神道の形成 |author-link=井上順孝}}</ref>
His thought blurred the lines between monotheism and polytheism, entering [[:en:Transtheism|transtheism]].<ref name=":0" /> Sano's concept of kami was aimed at resisting the propagation of Christianity while composing teachings that were in line with the aims of popular national indoctrination. His core elements of the concept of kami did not change throughout his life.<ref name=":0" />
He believed the etymology of [[Kami]] was derived from {{Nihongo|vital force|Ikimochi}}. He saw this as emphasizing the interconnectedness of everything from humans to nature, and as such this could be intereted as a monotheistic view.<ref name=":0" /> He saw all the kami as unified under a divine principle, hence the name of the group.<ref name=":0" />
==Overview==
{{Infobox organization | name = Shinrikyō | image = Shinrikyo_kyomon.svg | image_size = 120px | caption = Emblem of Shinrikyō, the sun, moon, and five-star crest said to have been granted by Emperor Yūryaku<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sinri.or.jp/page/mae.html|title=神理教の大教殿前|publisher=神理教|accessdate=2012-08-20}}</ref> | image2 = Shinrikyo02.jpg | image_size2 = 280px | caption2 = Main shrine of Shinrikyō | map2 = {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E}}}} | founded = 1884 | type = {{ill|Religious corporation|ja|宗教法人|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Religious corporation|qq=}} | headquarters = [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]][[:en:Kitakyushu|Kitakyushu]][[:en:Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyūshū|Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu]]{{ill|Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|ja|徳力|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|qq=|1=Tokuriki (Kitakyushu)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11489547}} 5-10-8 | coords = {{coord|33|49|33.5|N|130|51|52.9|E|display=inline,title}} | founder = {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=|1=Tsunehiko Sano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385093}} | website = [http://www.sinri.or.jp/ Shinrikyō]{{Ja icon}} }}
'''Shinrikyō''' (神理教) is a sect of [[:en:Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto]] founded by {{ill|Sano Tsunehiko|ja|佐野経彦|lt=Kannagibe Tsunehiko|lt_ja=巫部経彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sano Tsunehiko|qq=|1=Tsunehiko Sano|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11385093}} based on the traditional ''Kannagibe Shintō'' (巫部神道). Primarily active around [[:en:Ogura (disambiguation)|Kokura]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] on [[:en:Kyushu|Kyushu]], Shinrikyō disseminated teachings of [[:en:Ko-Shintō|Koshintō]].
== Overview == Shinrikyō traces its lineage to {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}} through the Kannagibe genealogy{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=226}}{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}. Founded officially in 1884 after receiving initial permission as Shinrikyōkai from the Shintō Secretariat in 1880, it became independent from [[:en:Ontake-kyō|Ontake-kyō]] in 1894. Since June 14, 1952, it has been registered as a religious corporation under Japanese law{{sfn|井上順孝ほか編|1996|p=134}}.
It venerates eighteen heavenly deities, classified as ''Amenimasu Moromoro no Kami'' (天在諸神), from [[:en:Ame-no-Minakanushi|Ame-no-Minakanushi]] to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照皇太神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天照大神}}. According to Japan's Agency for Cultural Affairs, Shinrikyō belongs to the [[:en:Fukko Shinto|Restoration Shintō]] category within Sect Shintō{{sfn|文化庁編さん|2011|pp=5-6}}.
== Kannagibe Shintō == Sano inherited family records tracing back to Nigihayahi, becoming the 77th generation{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-155}}. He developed Shinrikyō based on these traditions.
===Kannagibe lineage=== 1.{{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}, 2.{{ill|Umashimaji|ja|宇麻志麻知命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umashimaji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, (continued lineage up to) 77. Sano Tsunehiko{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=150-151}}.
== Founding of Shinrikyōkai == In 1877, Sano began preaching publicly and founded Shinrikyōkai officially in 1880. After gaining recognition from imperial princes and unsuccessful attempts to acquire sacred relics from Ise Shrine, it became independent in 1894.
== Teachings and Features == The primary doctrine appears in the "Shinrizu" (神理図), focusing on cosmology, ethics, and divine influence on human life{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|pp=214-220}}.
===Deities=== Primary eighteen gods include Amenominakanushi, Takamimusubi, Kamimusubi, and Amaterasu. Others revered include Tsukuyomi and Susanoo{{sfn|井上順孝|1991|p=229}}.
===Organization and Expansion=== Headquarters remain in Kitakyushu. At its peak in 1906, it claimed 1.5 million adherents. Today it has 31,945 followers{{sfn|文化庁『宗教年鑑 令和6年版』|p=61}}.
== Leadership == * First leader: Sano Tsunehiko * Current (fifth) leader: Kannagibe Sukehiko (巫部祐彦)
== Headquarters == Tokuriki 5-10-8, Kokuraminami-ku, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Access == * Nishitetsu Bus Kitakyushu, Shinrikyō-mae stop * Kitakyushu Monorail, Tokuriki Arashiyamaguchi Station
== Publications == Monthly journal: "Shinri," established in 1912.
